brief: The allotment block is empty for a quarter of the year: `allotRate = (0.01 + 0.16*ripePlots()/17) * (raining ? 0.2 : 1)` (~5630) and ripePlots() is 0 all winter, so the 0.01 floor sends nobody for ~six sim days and the plots sit under snow with nothing happening in them. Give the block a winter: on mild, dry, daylit winter days (warmth low, !raining, snowCover < 0.3) a gardener comes to a FALLOW plot (bAge as the fallow clock, `harvestPlot`, `plotCrop`) and turns it — an `act:'dig'` stop of a few seconds — and the plot reads as freshly turned earth (a darker, rowless state through `groundCol`/the plot draw) until the spring sowing. Hardy cabbages (`plotStands`) stand through it as they do now.
successLooksLike: allot-year.mjs folded over two years: gardener visits in winter weeks go from ~0 to a small steady rate (1–3 per sim day on dry mild days, 0 in snow or rain), with the summer rate unchanged. A late-winter shot shows two or three dark turned plots among the white/fallow ones; the same instant on HEAD is uniform. Census planting.harvested unchanged.
avoid: Do not change ripePlots() or the harvest cycle. Keep the winter gardener on spawnAllotAgent's own source (it exists so the block does not compete for laneCap). One new per-plot state at most.
